clue.text: Party as part of special event is in need of a lot of work

definitions.text: in need of a lot of work

parts.note: the Labour Party, one of Britain's two main political parties

indicators.note: something special is out of the ordinary, so the following letters leave their usual order

parts.note: to be in something is to be part of it

explanation.surface: A party held as part of some special occasion turns out to demand a great deal of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: LABOUR is the British left-of-centre party; 'special' looks like it describes the event but it rearranges 'event is' into TENSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Work that is labour-intensive demands much human effort, as opposed to machinery or capital.

clue.text: Enraptured about church still

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word for church is read backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone rapt with joy over a church that stands silent and unmoving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sits between definition and church, so it looks like a link word; it turns the church abbreviation round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person carried away by overwhelming delight or rapture.

clue.text: Grave disease consuming old man

indicators.note: something consuming another swallows it up, so the disease word wraps around the old man

explanation.surface: A serious illness is wasting away an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like an adjective (serious disease) but is the noun for a burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomb is a burial place for the dead, the same as a grave in noun sense.

clue.text: Setter involved in RAC road trip's given music device

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters fall over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The puzzle-setter, on a motoring trip with the RAC, is handed something to play music on.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British breakdown service; here its letters just join the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio fitted in a vehicle is a device for listening to music while driving.

clue.text: Spread fear about cheat in a brimmed hat

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the cheat word
spread suggests something scattered about, so the letters of the fear word are mixed up

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them

explanation.surface: Someone in a broad-brimmed hat is spreading fear about a swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: To do someone, in British slang, is to cheat or swindle them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a brim and creased crown.

clue.text: Heartlessly takes dodgy chance to be a star

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the following word is removed
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the remaining letters are put out of order

parts.note: the word with its central letter K removed
a risk is a chance taken

explanation.surface: A gambler cynically takes a shady chance in hope of stardom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity, but here it is the printed symbol *.
explanation.definitionFit: The asterisk is the small star-shaped typographic symbol; its name comes from Greek for little star.

clue.text: Meal's about done

parts.note: something done is over and past

explanation.surface: A dinner is just about finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal or literary word for a meal or the food eaten at one.

clue.text: Way to go for a job with commitment and class

definitions.text: Way to go for a job

parts.note: application is diligent effort and commitment
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Advice that the way to land a job is to show dedication and style.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Filling in the official document is the standard means of seeking employment.

clue.text: Change oar arrangement to reach harbour

indicators.note: an arrangement sets things in a new order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A rower is told to alter the oars to get into port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like the instruction but it is fodder; the shuffle is signalled by 'arrangement'.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorage is a sheltered place where ships can lie at anchor, much like a port.

clue.text: Sooty's pal Soo's beginning to cry

indicators.note: the beginning of a name is its opening letter only

explanation.surface: Childrens' puppet show: the pal of Sooty watching Soo start to sob.
explanation.walkthrough: Sooty is a British children's TV glove-puppet bear; Sweep is his dog friend and Soo his panda friend.
explanation.definitionFit: In the long-running British puppet show, the squeaky grey dog is the bear Sooty's closest companion.

clue.text: Time of year for company return to be run

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the company abbreviation is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: R for run in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A business announces when in the year it will make a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth calendar month is a period in the annual cycle, an autumn month in the north.

clue.text: Comprehensive is gone and Academy is taking students

parts.note: L is a learner driver; two of them for students

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school has closed and an academy now takes in its pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain comprehensives and academies are both kinds of state secondary school; 'Comprehensive' here means all-embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: An overall view takes in everything, the sense of all-inclusive or total.

clue.text: Picked up legal documents for posh hotel

indicators.note: picked up as in heard on a radio or by ear, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: writs are formal written court orders

explanation.surface: Someone collected legal papers for a smart hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz is a famously luxurious London hotel whose name became a byword for opulence.

clue.text: Utopian cities laid waste

indicators.note: laid waste means wrecked, so these letters are torn apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Perfect towns of a dreamer's vision destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid waste' reads as one phrase, but 'laid' is fodder and 'waste' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe visions of a perfect society that are unrealistically hopeful.

clue.text: I am unable to get even mains in new condo

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the combined letters take a new order
even means only the letters in even-numbered positions are kept

parts.note: second and fourth letters of mains

explanation.surface: A resident complains that electricity cannot be connected in a newly built apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: A condo, short for condominium, is an apartment; mains is the household supply of power.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is an informal pidgin-style refusal meaning that something is impossible for the speaker.

clue.text: Join queue to get something for a manicure

parts.note: to nail is to fasten pieces together
a file is a line of people one behind another

explanation.surface: Instructions to line up for a beauty treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A small abrasive tool for shaping fingernails is a basic item used in manicures.

clue.text: Shabby trunk emptied contents

indicators.note: contents are what lies inside, so the letters are found within the preceding words

parts.note: letters three to nine of these words

explanation.surface: A battered old trunk has had everything inside it emptied out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emptied' hints at removing contents, yet the answer sits inside trUNK EMPTied.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an untidy, neglected appearance, especially of clothes or hair.

clue.text: It's obvious, but sun damage has beginnings of lasting effects

indicators.note: damage breaks things apart, so the preceding letters are rearranged
the beginnings of words are their first letters only

parts.note: first letters of lasting and effects

explanation.surface: A warning that sunburn leaves lasting marks, which is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' looks like a connecting word, yet its letters join the sun in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsubtle is crude and heavy-handed, lacking any delicacy, so it is plain to see.

clue.text: Rising Cam before long draws in a thousand fish

indicators.note: to draw in is to take inside, so the thousand goes within the rest
in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the river name runs backwards

parts.note: the Cam, the river through Cambridge
ere is an old word for before
L is the abbreviation for long

explanation.surface: A rising river in Cambridge pulls in a vast shoal of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before long' reads as 'soon', but it splits into ERE and L. The Cam is Cambridge's river.
explanation.definitionFit: The mackerel is a striped oily sea fish common around British coasts.

clue.text: Heard I could be wisest to hide name of person at the scene

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: the pronoun sounds like the organ of sight

indicators.note: to hide something is to put it inside, so the name abbreviation goes within the other letters
could be suggests a possible alternative form, so these letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rumour that the smartest thing might be to keep a name secret, said about a witness at a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyewitness is someone who was present and saw an event, especially a crime.

clue.text: Provide endless space to raise a horse

definitions.note: equine used as a noun, a member of the horse family

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the provide word is dropped

parts.note: equip, to provide, without its last letter

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means lifting upwards, so the space word reads backwards

parts.note: an en is a printing space

explanation.surface: Instructions to give unlimited room to rear a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's space half the width of an em.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an equine is any animal of the horse family.

clue.text: A vine cultivated over time becomes indigenous

indicators.note: cultivated means worked over and tended, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A grapevine grown for long enough comes to belong to the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a plant or creature originating naturally in a particular region.

clue.text: E-copy?

parts.note: surface reading: an electronic copy of a document
setter's reading: the NATO code word for the letter E, which also means a copy of a sound bouncing back

explanation.walkthrough: The e- prefix looks like electronic; instead E is the letter whose radio alphabet name is the answer, and that word also means a repeated sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a reflected repetition of a sound, a copy; it is also the phonetic alphabet name for E.

clue.text: Pass on advice for putting out candle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for to die
second meaning: an instruction to extinguish the flame

explanation.surface: Passing on some tips for blowing out a candle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass on' suggests handing over advice, but it is a euphemism for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for dying, and literally tells someone to extinguish a flame by pinching or capping it.

clue.text: Field behind cove has fine ingredient for a stew

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the field word follows the cove word

parts.note: a cove is a small bay
a lea is a meadow or field

explanation.surface: A meadow behind a coastal inlet holds a good thing to add to stews.
explanation.definitionFit: The aromatic dried leaf of the laurel tree is a common herb added to casseroles and stews.

clue.text: American ox's crossing point

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the ox word spans the point

parts.note: a yak is a Tibetan ox

explanation.surface: A place where cattle ford a river in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Yank is informal slang for an American, especially used by Britons.

clue.text: Very trendy young lady's first record

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the lady word is used

explanation.surface: A fashionable girl's debut album.
explanation.definitionFit: Records are pressed from the plastic, so the material's name stands for a record or LP itself.

clue.text: Layabout lout never one to offer help freely

indicators.note: a layabout lies about, so the following letters are lying about in disorder

explanation.surface: An idle yob is never the type to pitch in and help for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layabout' looks like a noun describing the lout, but read as lay about it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A volunteer is a person who freely offers to do something, often unpaid.
